00148 /**
00149  * @brief               Hide the cursor until the user moves it again
00150  *
00151  * This function will hide the cursor until it is moved by the user.
00152  * This is usually used when processing keyboard or wheel events to make
00153  * the cursor get out of the way of the user while they are using the
00154  * device by an alternate means.  Internally, this sets a flag in the
00155  * window manager that hides the cursor from the screen, but any input
00156  * from the user will unhide it.
00157  *
00158  * The cursor is warped to the widget's location plus the x,y offset.
00159  * This is useful for directing mouse events to a particular control.
00160  * When the mouse is moved, it will be restored to it's original
00161  * location by the window manager.
00162  * 
00163  * @param pWidget              NULL if cursor should stay in same position, or
00164  *                             pointer to widget or window to use as coordinate
00165  *                             base for mouse button events
00166  * @param x                    x offset from top-left of pWidget or 0
00167  * @param y                    y offset from top-left of pWidget or 0
00168  * @return HxResult:           Returns HX_OK if succesful.
00169  **/
00170 HxResult HxCursorHideUntilMoved(HxWidget_t *pWidget, int32_t x, int32_t y);
00171 
00172 /**
00173  * @brief               Check if the cursor has been hidden pending movement
00174  *
00175  * This function will return the hidden status of the cursor.  This will
00176  * be true if there had been a call to HxCursorHideUntilMoved and the user
00177  * had not yet touched the trackpoint or mouse to move the cursor.
00178  * 
00179  * @param pHidden              Points to hidden value of cursor
00180  * @return HxResult:           Returns HX_OK if succesful, 
00181  *                             HX_NULL_POINTER if pHidden is NULL.
00182  **/
00183 HxResult HxCursorGetHidden(bool *pHidden);

00216 /**
00217  * @brief               Set the cursor's location
00218  *
00219  * HxCursorSetPosition sets the cursor location.  The coordinates are relative
00220  * to the display, not to the windows.
00221  *
00222  * If (x, y) is set to (0, 0), for example, the cursor is drawn at the top
00223  * left corner of the application bar.
00224  *
00225  * If x < 0, cursor's x coordinate is set to 0, and no error is returned.
00226  * If y < 0, cursor's y coordinate is set to 0, and no error is returned.
00227  * If x > display width, x is set to display width, and no error is returned.
00228  * If x > display height, x is set to display height, and no error is returned.
00229  *
00230  * @param x               IN:  x coordinate
00231  * @param y               IN:  y coordinate
00232  *
00233  * @return HxResult:           Returns HX_OK.
00234  *
00235  **/
